Bowlbugs.wikitext:
The '''Bowlbugs''' are a group of normal {{2|Monsters|Enemies}} found in the {{2|Hive}}. Each encounter features a Bowlbug (Rock) alongside 1 or 2 worker bowlbugs chosen from Egg, Silk, and Nectar types. Individual bowlbugs also appear alongside {{2|Tunneler}} and {{2|Slumbering Beetle}}.

== Bowlbug (Rock) ==
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Bowlbug (Rock)
|Image  = StS2_Bowlbug (Rock).png
|HP     = 45-48
|AscHP  = 46-49
|Powers = {{BD2|Imbalanced}}
|Debut  = Hive
|Type   = Normal
}} {{Power Infobox|Imbalanced|2}}
=== Pattern ===
{{Intents Table/start|Bowlbug (Rock)}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Headbutt
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|16}}) damage.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Dizzy
|Intent = Stun
|Effect = Stunned. Does nothing.}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
Uses {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt||2}} every turn. However, if {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt||2}}'s damage is fully prevented by a player, the Bowlbug (Rock) becomes {{KW2|Stunned}} and uses {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Dizzy||2}} on its next turn, then resumes {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt||2}}.

=== Notes ===
* The in-game description of {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is somewhat misleading. The Bowlbug (Rock) will become {{KW2|Stunned}} as long as the player has at least 1 {{KW2|Block}} and {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt|Headbutt's|2}} damage is fully prevented. Some other methods of preventing damage are:
** Playing {{BD2|Buffer}}.
** Reducing the Bowlbug (Rock)'s {{BD2|Strength}}.
** Blocking all but 1 damage and preventing that 1 damage with {{R2|Tungsten Rod}}.
* If attack is reduced to 0 (For example via {{C2|Mangle}}), but player has no block Bowlbug (Rock) will not be stunned.
* If {{KW2|Osty}} takes damage from {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt||2}}, it will not become {{KW2|Stunned}}.
* Since {{BD2|Imbalanced}} is a debuff, {{C2|Misery}} can apply it to other enemies in the fight.
* In {{2|Multiplayer}}, only one player needs to fully block {{Int|Bowlbug (Rock)|Headbutt||2}} to {{KW2|Stunned|Stun}} the Bowlbug (Rock).

Ceremonial Beast.wikitext:
{{Enemy Infobox
|Name   = Ceremonial Beast
|Image  = StS2_Ceremonial Beast.png
|Icon   = StS2 Icon CeremonialBeastBoss.png
|HP     = 252
|AscHP  = 262
|Debut  = Overgrowth
|Type   = Boss
}} {{Power Infobox|Plow|2}} {{Power Infobox|Ringing|2}}
'''Ceremonial Beast''' is a {{2|Bosses|Boss}} found in the {{2|Overgrowth}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Ceremonial Beast}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Stamp
|Intent = Buff
|Effect = Gains {{BD2|Plow}} (150;{{Asc2|9|160}}). When its HP drops to that amount, it becomes {{BD2|Stunned}} and loses all {{BD2|Strength}}.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Plow
|Intent = Attack3, Buff
|Effect = Deals (18;{{Asc2|9|20}}) damage. Gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Stun
|Intent = Stun
|Effect = Stunned. Does nothing.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Beast Cry
|Intent = Debuff
|Effect = Applies 1 {{BD2|Ringing}}.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Stomp
|Intent = Attack3
|Effect = Deals (15;{{Asc2|9|17}}) damage.}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Crush
|Intent = Attack3, Buff
|Effect = Deals (17;{{Asc2|9|19}}) damage. Gains (3;{{Asc2|9|4}}) {{BD2|Strength}}.}}
{{Intents Table/end}}
The Ceremonial Beast has two distinct phases.

'''Phase 1:'''
* Uses {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Stamp||2}} on the first turn, gaining {{BD2|Plow}}.
* Then uses {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Plow||2}} every turn.
When its HP drops to the {{BD2|Plow}} threshold (150, or {{Asc2|9|160}}), it immediately becomes {{BD2|Stunned}} and loses all {{BD2|Strength}}.

'''Phase 2:''' After being stunned, repeats this three-move cycle:
# {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Beast Cry||2}}
# {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Stomp||2}}
# {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Crush||2}}

== Notes ==
* {{BD2|Plow}} acts as a HP threshold: when the Ceremonial Beast's HP drops to the {{BD2|Plow}} amount or below, it is {{KW2|Stunned}} and loses all accumulated {{BD2|Strength}}. This effectively gives the player a free turn.
** If the Ceremonial Beast's HP is already below the {{BD2|Plow}} threshold on the first turn (before it gains {{BD2|Plow}}), it will not become {{KW2|Stunned}} when it gains {{BD2|Plow}}. Instead, it acts normally until it loses any amount of HP, which will trigger the {{BD2|Plow}} effect like normal.
* {{BD2|Ringing}} from {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Beast Cry||2}} limits the player to playing only 1 card on that turn.
* During Phase 1, each {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Plow||2}} gains 2 {{BD2|Strength}}, but all of it is lost when the Ceremonial Beast's HP drops to the {{BD|Plow||}} threshold. In Phase 2, each {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Crush||2}} gains 3 ({{Asc|9|4}}) {{BD2|Strength}} that accumulates for the rest of the battle.

==Useful Cards==
===Synergies===
* {{BD2|Block Next Turn}} ({{C2|Dodge and Roll}}, {{C2|Glitterstream}}, and {{C2|Prolong}}) can mitigate {{BD|Ringing|Ringing's|2}} card play limit.
** {{BD2|Barricade}} and {{R2|Sturdy Clamp}} can provide a similar benefit.
* Cards which can apply multiple stacks of {{BD2|Weak}}, such as {{C2|Leg Sweep}} or {{C2|Uppercut|Uppercut+}}, can be played on the turn that '''Ceremonial Beast''' uses  {{Int|Ceremonial Beast|Beast Cry||2}}. This will lower its damage on the next turn while still allowing another card to be played.

===Anti-Synergies===
* Effects that automatically play cards (such as {{C2|Hellraiser}}, {{C2|Mayhem}}, or {{C2|Bombardment}}) can consume the singular card play permitted by {{BD2|Ringing}}. 
** Similarly, {{C2|Stampede|Stampede's}} triggered {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack|2}} will not be played if the player already played another card this turn.
* {{BD2|Ringing}} makes cards that ''generate other cards'' to be played (such as {{C2|Infernal Blade}}, {{C2|Quasar}}, and {{C2|Discovery}}) effectively useless.
* {{BD2|Ringing}} prevents {{BD2|Echo Form}} from copying the first card played.
* {{BD2|Ringing}} prevents {{KW2|Sly}} cards from playing if they were discarded by another card's effect.
** If the {{KW2|Sly}} card is discarded by an effect on the player (e.g. {{BD2|Tools of the Trade}}) or by {{P2|Gambler's Brew}}, it will be played as normal. However, it will count towards {{BD|Ringing|Ringing's|2}} limit this turn.

== Trivia ==
* {{R2|Blessed Antler}} is likely an antler from a Ceremonial Beast. In the battle with the Ceremonial Beast, multiple other ghostly skulls are present, some with missing antlers.
** {{R|Blessed Antler|Blessed Antler's|2}} creation of {{C2|Dazed}} cards likely references the {{BD2|Ringing}} status: both of these effects limit how many cards can be played ({{BD2|Ringing}} imposes a hard limit, while {{C2|Dazed}} cards are {{KW2|Unplayable}}).

** However, the speech bubble is immediately obscured by the three {{C2|Dazed}} appearing (especially when Fast Mode is enabled).

* '''Personal Hive''' triggers whever the '''Entomancer''' takes attack damage, rather than whenever an attack is played. This means that it will trigger multiple times against cards like {{C2|Sword Boomerang}} or {{C2|Ricochet}}.

* Strong single-hit attacks like {{C2|Bludgeon}} or {{C2|Bury}} can deal a significant amount of damage while only triggering {{BD2|Personal Hive}}  once.
* {{BD2|Strength}} reduction from cards like {{C2|Malaise}} can greatly lower the damage from {{Int|Entomancer|Beeeees!||2}}.
* Cards like {{C2|Feel No Pain}} or {{C2|Compact}} can turn the {{C2|Dazed}} cards into a benefit.

'''Exoskeleton''' is a normal {{2|Monsters|Enemy}} found in {{2|Hive}}.

== Pattern ==
{{Intents Table/start|Exoskeleton}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Skitter
|Intent = Attack1
|Effect = Deals 1 damage (×3;{{Asc2|9|×4}}).}}
{{Intents Table/row
|Name   = Mandibles

{{Intents Table/end}}
Exoskeletons appear in groups of 3 or 4. Each one's opening move depends on its position in the group: 
* The first uses {{Int|Exoskeleton|Skitter||2}}
* The second uses {{Int|Exoskeleton|Mandibles||2}}
* The third uses {{Int|Exoskeleton|Enrage||2}}
* The fourth (if present) randomly picks {{Int|Exoskeleton|Skitter||2}} or {{Int|Exoskeleton|Mandibles||2}}.


* After {{Int|Exoskeleton|Skitter||2}}, the next move is randomly {{Int|Exoskeleton|Skitter||2}} or {{Int|Exoskeleton|Mandibles||2}} (cannot repeat the same move twice in a row). 
* After {{Int|Exoskeleton|Mandibles||2}}, it always uses {{Int|Exoskeleton|Enrage||2}}. 
* After {{Int|Exoskeleton|Enrage||2}}, the next move is randomly {{Int|Exoskeleton|Skitter||2}} or {{Int|Exoskeleton|Mandibles||2}}.

== In Party With ==
=== Hive ===
* 3 Exoskeletons (Weak)
* 4 Exoskeletons (Normal)

== Useful Cards ==

* Large amounts of {{BD2|Strength}} or expensive, high-damage cards like {{C2|Bludgeon}} are less effective than usual against the '''Exoskeletons''', as each hit is capped at 9 damage no matter how much it would normally deal.
* Multihitting attacks like {{C2|Sword Boomerang}} can benefit more than other cards from '''Strength''' because each hit can individually deal up to 9 damage.
* Attacks like {{C2|Breakthrough}} or {{C2|Crush Under}} can hit all enemies at once, and those like {{C2|Dagger Spray}} or {{C2|Conflagration}} which do small amounts of multiple times can benefit more from {{BD2|Strength}} or other damage boosts without hitting the damage cap.
* Any source of {{KW2|Doom}} can bypass the damage cap, as it simply kills enemies at end of turn rather than damaging them. The "Kill enemies" effect on {{C2|End of Days}} will similarly ignore '''Hard to Kill'''.
* {{BD2|Thorns}} from cards like {{C2|Abrasive}} will deal damage each time any of the '''Exoskeletons''' attack, and multiple times when they use '''Skitter'''.

After the third {{Int|Knowledge Demon|Curse of Knowledge||2}} (once all three status sets have been offered), the cycle changes: {{Int|Knowledge Demon|Curse of Knowledge||2}} is skipped, and the remaining three moves repeat in order.

== Notes ==
* {{Int|Knowledge Demon|Curse of Knowledge||2}} status sets:
** Set 1: {{BD2|Disintegration}} (6 damage/turn) or {{BD2|Mind Rot}} (draw 1 fewer card/turn)
** Set 2: {{BD2|Disintegration}} (7 damage/turn) or {{BD2|Sloth}} (max 3 cards/turn)
** Set 3: {{BD2|Disintegration}} (8 damage/turn) or {{BD2|Waste Away}} (1 less {{KW2|Energy}}/turn)
* The debuffs from {{Int|Knowledge Demon|Curse of Knowledge||2}} are shown as cards, but are never added to the player's hand or deck. Once chosen, they are instantly played and removed from the game.

== Useful Cards ==
* In order to deal with the extra damage from {{BD2|Disintegration}}, you can either use strong defensive cards like {{C2|Footwork}} or {{C2|Feel No Pain}}, or simply enter the battle with a significant HP pool and finish off the '''Knowledge Demon''' before it can kill you. If you cannot afford to take this extra damage, it may be a good idea to take cards which make the other options less harmful.
* Strength reduction from cards like {{C2|Piercing Wail}} or {{C2|Monarch's Gaze}} can make multihitting attacks much less deadly.
* Strong draw from cards like {{C2|Acrobatics}} or {{C2|Machine Learning}} can make {{BD2|Mind Rot}} less impactful.
* {{R2|Runic Pyramid}} makes {{BD2|Mind Rot}} significantly less of a problem by saving cards from previous turns.
* {{C2|Pyre}} can make up for the energy loss from {{BD2|Waste Away}}.
* Strong, expensive cards like {{C2|Impervious}} and {{C2|Ice Lance}} are an effective way to use your limited card plays after taking {{BD2|Sloth}}.
* The {{R2|Pocketwatch}} can help make up for the limited draw from {{BD2|Mind Rot}}, and as long as you are already playing only 3 cards per turn to activate it, {{BD2|Sloth}} is essentially harmless.

Phrog Parasite alternates between its two moves:
# {{Int|Phrog Parasite|Infect||2}}
# {{Int|Phrog Parasite|Lash||2}}
# Back to {{Int|Phrog Parasite|Infect||2}}, and so on.

When Phrog Parasite dies, {{BD2|Infested}} triggers and 4 {{M|Wriggler|Wrigglers|2}} are summoned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} and do nothing on their first turn. The fight continues until all Wrigglers are defeated.

== Notes ==
* Whether the Wrigglers are {{KW2|Stunned}} on the player's next turn depends on if the Phrog Parasite dies during the player turn or the enemy turn:
** If the Phrog Parasite is killed with an Attack card or damage from an Orb, the Wrigglers will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during this turn, ''not'' the player's next turn.
** If the Phrog Parasite dies to {{BD2|Poison}} or {{KW2|Doom}}, then the Wrigglers will have no {{2|Intent}} when spawned. They will be {{KW2|Stunned}} during the player's next turn.
*** This also applies if the Phrog Parasite dies as a result of its own attack, such as by {{BD2|Thorns}} or {{C2|Necro Mastery}}.
<!--
Confirm this is all correct, I've tested but may have missed something or made a mistake
-->
* '''Infections''' deal damage during the player turn, so the damage will activate cards like {{C2|Inferno}} or {{C2|Rupture}}.
* {{C2|Omnislice}} damages the target, then damages all other enemies afterwards. If the first hit kills the '''Phrog Parasite''', then it will spawn '''Wrigglers''' before the card resolves and the Wrigglers will also take damage.

== Useful Cards ==
* Frontloaded damage cards like {{C2|Perfected Strike}}, {{C2|Backstab}}, and {{C2|Defile}} can be useful for taking down the Phrog Parasite before it can create too many Infections. They can also finish off individual Wrigglers quickly.
* {{C2|Deathbringer}}, {{C2|Deadly Poison}}, and other cards which apply {{BD2|Poison}} or {{KW2|Doom}} can gain an extra turn before the Wrigglers attack, if the Phrog Parasite dies to their damage.
* Attacks which target all enemies like {{C2|Dagger Spray}}, {{C2|Bone Shards}}, and {{C2|Whirlwind}} can damage all of the Wrigglers at once.
* {{C2|Inferno}} deals consistent damage to all enemies every turn. It also triggers whenever '''Infections''' deal unblocked damage.
* Cards which can discard, {{KW2|Exhaust}}, or {{KW2|Transform}} '''Infections''', such as {{C2|Burning Pact}} or {{C2|Hidden Daggers}}, can prevent them from dealing damage.
** {{C2|Compact}} and {{C2|Flak Cannon}} are especially noteworthy, since they remove all '''Infections''' in Hand or in all zones, respectively.

== Trivia ==
* The {{R2|Paper Phrog}} is likely based on the same type of creature being {{BD2|Infested}} by the Phrog Parasite.

V0.111.0 - Beta Patch.title: Slay the Spire 2:V0.111.0 - Beta Patch
V0.111.0 - Beta Patch.wikitext:
{{PatchNav
|Version = V0.111.0
|ReleaseDate = 2026-08-13
|Type = Beta Patch
}}

Time for another beta patch! Heads up that there won't be a patch on the 27th as our team is taking a break in the last week of August. As we'll explain a bit further in the upcoming August Neowsletter, there may be a longer wait in general for the next patch, as we've shifted our focus to some BIG, much-anticipated pieces of content!

In the meantime, let's look at some of this update's highlights. First off, there are a couple of card reworks and lots of various balance changes as well as UX and performance improvements. Also, we have officially implemented Indonesian localization! In the art and VFX realm, we've added some cool new card art and, excitingly, low HP idle animations for all of the playable characters! Now when you're close to death you'll at least have some fun visual flair to go along with it.

[[File:PatchNotes_LowHPAnimation.gif|frame|center]]
We look forward to hearing all of your feedback! Now on with the rest of the patch notes...

== CONTENT & BALANCE ==
=== Ancients: ===
* Nerfed Tezcatara's Brightest Flame card: max HP loss increased from 1 -> 2
* Nerfed Nonupeipe's Beautiful Bracelet relic: now Enchants 4 random cards instead of allowing you to select the cards to Enchant
	
=== Enemies: ===
* Buffed Axebot:
** Hammer Uppercut move damage increased from 12(14) → 14(18)
** Now gains +10 Max HP each time it respawns
** The One-Two damage from 9(10)x2 → 10(11)x2

* Buffed Mechaknight: now also deals 8(12) damage on its Flamethrower turn
* Buffed Exoskeleton: HP at A8 increased from 24-28(25-29) → 24-28(26-30)
* Buffed Globe Head: Galvanic power at A9 increased from 6(6) → 6(8)
* Buffed Louse Progenitor: Strength gain at A9 increased from 5(5) → 5(7)
* Buffed Soul Fysh: De-Gas move damage at A9 increased from 16(17) → 16(18)
* (''Unlisted change'') Buffed Entomancer: HP at A8 increased from 145(155) → 145(165)

=== Colorless Cards: ===
*Changed Rend card:
**Energy cost decreased from 2 → 1
**Base damage decreased from 15(18) → 10(12)

*Changed Salvo and Splash cards: swapped rarities, Splash is now Rare and Salvo is now Uncommon

=== Ironclad: ===
*Reworked Expect a Fight card: from Uncommon - Skill - Cost 2(1) - "Gain 1 Energy for each Attack in your Hand. You cannot gain additional Energy this turn." → Uncommon - Skill - Cost 3 - "Gain 15(16) Block. Gains 5(8) additional Block for each Strength you have."
*Buffed Forgotten Ritual card: no longer requires a card to be Exhausted to gain Energy
*Buffed Rampage card:
**Base damage increased from 9 → 10
**Scaling damage from 5(9) → 5(10)

=== Silent: ===
*Nerfed Blade of Ink card: Inky enchantment no longer gives additional damage (still applies Weak)
*Nerfed Mirage card: now Exhausts and loses Exhaust on upgrade instead of cost lowering from 1 → 0

=== Regent: ===
*Buffed Alignment card: Star cost decreased from 3 → 2
*Buffed Spoils of Battle card: Forge increased from 5(8) → 6(9)
*Nerfed Refine Blade card: Forge decreased from 9(13) → 8(12)
* (''Unlisted change'') Changed Guiding Star card:
** Card draw changed from this turn → next turn
** Star cost decreased from 2 → 1
*Nerfed Regalite relic: Block gain decreased from 6 → 4

=== Necrobinder: ===
*Buffed Shroud card: Block gain increased from 2(3) → 3(4)
*Buffed Time's Up card: no longer has Exhaust

=== Defect: ===
*Reworked Hyperbeam card: from "Deal 30(38) damage to ALL enemies. Lose 3 Focus." → "Deal 24(30) damage to ALL enemies. Lose 3 Focus this turn."
*Buffed Thunder card: Damage from 6(8) → 8(11)
*Nerfed Null card: Weak application decreased from 2(3) → 1(2)
*Nerfed Synchronize card: Focus decreased from 2(3) → 1(2)

== WRITING ==
*Added Indonesian localization with English fallback

== USER EXPERIENCE & INTERFACE ==
*Vakuu's Jeweled Mask relic now chooses a non-Innate power unless all powers in the player's deck are Innate
*Cards with on-end-turn effects are now played faster when there are many of them
*Invite button is shown when the overlay is disabled, and displays an error
*Made it so players can confirm card selection via E again
*Sped up Epoch unlock VFX if playing in fast mode

== ART ==
*Added portrait art for the cards:
**Hibernate
**One For All
**Cacophony
**Underworld
**Midnight

*Added low HP idle animations for all playable characters
*Updated Necrobinder's slash VFX
*Changed Dexterity Potion back to being green

== BUG FIXES ==
=== General: ===
*Saves are no longer copied to the modded save directory if a player declined mod loading, but left their mods installed
*Fixed an issue where unmodded saves were not copied for players who had previously declined mod loading
*Fixed input being blocked after clearing map drawings while in map drawing mode
*Fixed map drawings breaking when lines are cleared while a stroke is in progress
*Fixed a crash that could happen in multiplayer when selecting a relic at a treasure room
*Fixed a crash that could occasionally happen after closing and then re-opening the single-card inspection screen
*Fixed an error when a card finished moving to a pile after combat ended
*Fixed an error when a combat would end while cards were still shuffling
*Fixed an issue where badges earned at the end of a run could be lost if you left the game over screen early or had already earned every unlock
*Fixed focus not returning to cards after rerolling rewards on controller

=== Enemies: ===
*Fixed Form VFX not flipping when the player flips direction during the Kaiser Crab Combat
*Fixed the Lost and Forgotten monster's death particles continuing to play the animation is interrupted in the Bestiary

=== Defect: ===
*Fixed Defect's power-up animation freezing when interrupted while playing Echo Form card

=== Multiplayer: ===
*Cacophony card no longer triggers a second time if its first trigger causes another card to be drawn (i.e. via Gremlin Horn relic)
*Unreadying in a loaded Daily Run lobby no longer leaves you readied up
*Fixed a multiplayer crash that could happen when killing the last enemy in an encounter with The Ball card

== PERFORMANCE ==
*Reduced hitch on Punch Off and The Lantern Key events
*Reduced stuttering when text appears for the first time in Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai and Russian
*Preloaded only the glyphs the bold and italic faces can render
